title: Recently Watched "The Batman" And I Didn't Like It

commenti.body: I agree with you. I found the movie very forgettable and I didn't understand why it needed to be made. To me it looks like it is trying to copy the Christopher Nolan trilogy which was a masterpiece (overall).  To have a new Batman universe that fails to feel fresh new and different felt like an insult to Chris Nolan and I was actually kinda mad that audiences responded well to it.

Hey, I'm of a similar opinion.

I feel like the success of the Batman gives evidence to the hypothesis that audiences are willing to gobble up a very middle of the road, and, to me slightly disappointing, if it has the best possible cinematography (Greg Fraser) and production value.

I think for a thriller to be dull takes a special kind of vanity ( great novelistically complex movies use the 3-hour run time well-- see the Godfather)

Speaking as a Batman fanatic, I can say that the first 45 minutes or so were film nirvana (no pun intended). The look and mood were perfect. But it definitely bit off more than it could chew after that. The Wayne backstory stuff never goes anywhere interesting and Selina’s subplot, while thematically fitting, feels shoehorned. By the - admittedly impressive - final in the arena you’re exhausted. 

Still, curious to see where it goes.

I just questioned the need to make another version of the same story. It’s starting from a fundamentally boring position, just making Batman a bit of a gothic edgelord and wasn’t interesting enough for me

This movie didn’t engage me from a story level in really any way. I couldn’t tell if the plot didn’t make sense or if I just didn’t care enough to pay attention. 

I will say that I enjoyed the atmosphere of the film, and the first 20 minutes or so was genuinely great, just had a cool set up. From there it kind of felt like a Fincher rip off. I did like this portrayal of Batman, reminded me of Clint Eastwood or Road Warrior era Mad Max. The silent protagonist thing works well for Batman imo. 

But yeah it just didn’t do much outside of set a cool mood. Also catwoman was basically just “girl” which is becoming increasingly more annoying in mainstream films. Thought they would have finally done something more interesting with the character but nope.
Just saw the new Top Gun a few days ago and this describes that exactly as well. But even I found myself having to hack through the images to see that it's a really standard, almost dull, movie.

There are some good ideas in there but the actual film is a bit of a mess and turns into an overlong slog at the end.

It really should have been two tight films, instead of one overstuffed narrative pushing three hours. End the first film with a triumphant bust of the Penguin, turning his club into an exciting setpiece and culminating in that highway chase, but ending on a cliffhanger when Penguin reveals he’s not the man behind the murders. So Bats and Gordon get a big victory but the story is still escalating.

Then dedicate the second film to the Riddler’s increasingly destructive attacks—and actually foreshadowing the flood maneuver, which comes out of complete nowhere in the existing film—while pushing Falcone’s story to the front as the contained narrative for this film.

It’s not a simple matter of cutting the existing film in two, but all the pieces and ideas are there. They’re just rushed or undeveloped.
Why is any movie made? To make money......

“With an 7.8 imdb rating and a great movie trailer, I was really hyped”

Lol. This really got me.

Same the Nolan ones really it was trying too hard and taking itself too seriously to be much fun, but too dumb to be taken that seriously either. I liked bits of it, or at least the intention of it, but it felt muddled in what it was trying to be/do/say. 

Paul Dano is generally amazing, and reinventing the Riddler as a 4chan edgelord is quite an interesting idea, but it just didn’t land for me. The ultra-violence seemed like it might be quite an impactful part of the story, but ended up just being a bit meaningless. 

The Nirvana stuff was just lame from the start.

My biggest gripe with the film is that the mystery man we’ve been searching for the entire movie, enduring edgelord clues and Seven-esque scenarios… is just a completely brand new and unannounced character. My hopes for an actual detective-style movie for the Worlds Greatest Detective were smashed. Nothing else about the movie was particularly remarkable, absolutely no new ground except throwing Bruce’s father into a moral grey area? It didn’t really cast Batman in a significantly different light or anything for me.

If anything, The Batman showcases why Gritty Wickian Batman has run its course. The major Batman villains are colorful and more than a bit ridiculous, like a ventriloquist gangster, or Riddler, who kills people with riddles ffs, but therein lies the charm. They’re so bizarre and interesting against Gotham’s drab backdrop. But nowadays, Penguin is simply Mob Boss With Pointy Nose, and Riddler is just, well, Seven. We’ve sacrificed everything interesting about these villains in exchange for realism, a realistic movie about a billionaire who dresses like a bat and fights crime. I’m absolutely glad we *tried* it with the Nolan movies, Ninja Swat Batman fight scenes are genuinely fun to watch, but I’m ready for something different.

The overuse of Nirvana’s “Something in the Way” was awful. It’s a fantastic song that is a complete mismatch for Batman. It’s also by a famous band and on a famous album—countless people had been listening to it for three decades by the time it came out and many already had long associations with it. 

Kurt Cobain was the voice of a generation and his personality is a huge part of Nirvana’s music. In a slow emotion filled song like “Something in the Way”, your thoughts are immediately directed to him and his suicide. Of course none of this has anything to do with Batman. 

Kurt Cobain’s art and resonates deeply with a large amount of people. Using it as the theme of the movie, repeated ad nauseam, was just a baffling choice.
On that note I’d like a foppish dandy joker again. Someone more John Waters than Sid Vicious.
